'''Jin-Quan Yu''' ({{zh|s=余金权|t=余金權|p=Yú Jīn-quán}}) is a Chinese-born American chemist. He is the Frank and Bertha Hupp Professor of Chemistry at [[Scripps Research]], where he also holds the [[Bristol Myers Squibb]] Endowed Chair in Chemistry.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Jennewein|first=Chris|date=2020-12-08|title=McArthur Fellow Jin-Quan Yu Named to Newly-Endowed Chemistry Chair|url=https://timesofsandiego.com/tech/2020/12/08/mcarthur-fellow-jin-quan-yu-named-to-newly-endowed-chemistry-chair/|access-date=2021-05-22|website=Times of San Diego|language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=Yu, Jin-Quan|url=https://vivo.scripps.edu/display/YuJinQuan|access-date=2021-05-22|website=vivo.scripps.edu|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Jin-Quan Yu {{!}} Scripps Research|url=https://www.scripps.edu/faculty/yu/|access-date=2021-05-22|website=www.scripps.edu}}</ref> He is a 2016 recipient of the [[MacArthur Fellows Program|MacArthur Fellowship]],<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|title=Jin-Quan Yu|url=https://www.macfound.org/fellows/class-of-2016/jin-quan-yu|access-date=2021-05-22|website=www.macfound.org|language=en}}</ref> and is a member of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]], [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]], and the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":4">{{Cite web|title=Jin-Quan Yu|url=https://www.amacad.org/person/jin-quan-yu|access-date=2021-05-22|website=American Academy of Arts & Sciences|language=en}}</ref> Yu is a leader in the development of [[Carbon–hydrogen bond activation|C–H bond activation]] reactions in organic chemistry, and has reported many C–H activation reactions that could be applicable towards the synthesis of drug molecules and other biologically active compounds. He also co-founded Vividion Therapeutics in 2016 with fellow Scripps chemists [[Benjamin Cravatt III|Benjamin Cravatt]] and [[Phil S. Baran|Phil Baran]],<ref>{{Cite web|title=Vividion Therapeutics: Creating a New Era in Drug Discovery|url=https://vividion.com/|access-date=2021-05-23|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Fikes|first=Bradley J.|title=Vividion Therapeutics to get $101 million upfront from alliance with Celgene|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/sd-me-vividion-raises-101-million-20180305-story.html|access-date=2021-05-23|website=chicagotribune.com}}</ref> and is a member of the scientific advisory board of Chemveda Life Sciences.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Scientific Advisory Board {{!}} Chemveda Life Sciences|url=http://chemvedals.com/advisory-board/|access-date=2021-05-23|language=en-US|archive-date=2021-05-23|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210523065730/http://chemvedals.com/advisory-board/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Yu was born on January 10, 1966, in [[Zhejiang|Zhejiang, China]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal|date=2011|title=Jin-Quan Yu|url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1002/anie.201101811|journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition|volume=50|issue=22|pages=5014|doi=10.1002/anie.201101811|issn=1521-3773|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Jin-Quan YU - Future Forum|url=https://www.futureforum.org.cn/en/people/512.html|access-date=2021-05-22|website=www.futureforum.org.cn}}</ref> He received his B.Sc. in chemistry at [[East China Normal University]] in 1987.<ref name=":1" /> Yu then went on to the Guangzhou Institute of Chemistry, [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] where he worked on [[Heterogeneous catalysis|heterogeneous reactions]] of [[Terpene|terpenes]] with [[zeolite]] materials with Prof. Shu-De Xiao, obtaining his M.Sc. in 1990.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Yu|first1=Jin-Quan|last2=Zhou|first2=Ping|last3=Xiao|first3=Shu-De|date=1995|title=Highly selective hydration reaction of α-pinene over H-mordenites pretreated with quaternary ammonium salts|url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1002/cjoc.19950130314|journal=Chinese Journal of Chemistry|language=en|volume=13|issue=3|pages=280–283|doi=10.1002/cjoc.19950130314|issn=1614-7065|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Bintang|first1=Liu|last2=Jinquan|first2=Yu|last3=Aiqun|first3=Eng|last4=Ping|first4=Zhou|last5=Shude|first5=Xiao|date=1995-06-25|title=Study on selective alkylation of guaiacol with camphene over H-Mordenite|url=http://sioc-journal.cn/Jwk_yjhx/EN/|journal=Chinese Journal of Organic Chemistry|language=en|volume=15|issue=3|pages=318|issn=0253-2786}}</ref> He remained at the Guangzhou Institute of Chemistry for four years as a research associate.{{citation needed|date=May 2021}}

In 1994, Yu moved to the [[United Kingdom]] to pursue graduate studies at the [[University of Cambridge]] with Prof. Jonathan B. Spencer.<ref name=":1" /> At Cambridge, he studied biosynthesis and the mechanistic details of the hydrometallation step in asymmetric [[hydrogenation]] reactions with [[Heterogeneous catalysis|heterogeneous]] and [[Homogeneous catalysis|homogeneous catalysts]], among the twenty-one papers he co-authored with Spencer.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Yu|first1=Jinquan|last2=Spencer|first2=Jonathan B.|date=1997|title=First Evidence That the Mechanism of Catalytic Hydrogenation with Homogeneous Palladium and Rhodium Catalysts Is Strongly Influenced by Substrate Polarity|url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/full/10.1021/ja964179i|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=119|issue=22|pages=5257–5258|doi=10.1021/ja964179i|bibcode=1997JAChS.119.5257Y |issn=0002-7863|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Spencer|first=Jinquan Yu and Jonathan B.|date=1997|title=Regioselective Hydrometalation of Alkenes Reveals the Amphipolar Nature of the Pd−H Bond in Heterogeneous Hydrogenation|url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/full/10.1021/jo971602c|journal=The Journal of Organic Chemistry|volume=62|issue=25|pages=8618–8619|doi=10.1021/jo971602c|issn=0022-3263|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Yu|first=Jinquan|date=1998-01-01|title=Discovery that quinoline and triphenylphosphine alter the electronic properties of hydrogenation catalysts|url=https://pubs.rsc.org/en/content/articlelanding/1998/cc/a800629f|journal=Chemical Communications|language=en|issue=10|pages=1103–1104|doi=10.1039/A800629F|issn=1364-548X|url-access=subscription}}</ref> Yu graduated with his Ph.D. in 1999.<ref name=":1" />

Between 1999 and 2001, Yu worked as a Junior Research Fellow of [[St John's College, Cambridge]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Yu|first1=Jinquan|last2=Gaunt|first2=Matthew J.|last3=Spencer|first3=Jonathan B.|date=2002|title=Convenient Preparation oftrans-Arylalkenes via Palladium(II)-Catalyzed Isomerization ofcis-Arylalkenes|url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/full/10.1021/jo015880u|journal=The Journal of Organic Chemistry|volume=67|issue=13|pages=4627–4629|doi=10.1021/jo015880u|pmid=12076172 |issn=0022-3263|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Yu|first1=Jin-Quan|last2=Wu|first2=Hai-Chen|last3=Ramarao|first3=Chandrashekar|last4=Spencer|first4=Jonathan B.|last5=Ley|first5=Steven V.|date=2003-01-01|title=Transfer hydrogenation using recyclable polyurea-encapsulated palladium: efficient and chemoselective reduction of aryl ketones|url=https://pubs.rsc.org/en/content/articlelanding/2003/cc/b300074p|journal=Chemical Communications|language=en|issue=6|pages=678–679|doi=10.1039/B300074P|pmid=12703769 |issn=1364-548X|url-access=subscription}}</ref> From 2001-2002, Yu worked as a postdoctoral fellow at [[Harvard University]] in the laboratory of Prof. [[Elias James Corey|E. J. Corey]] on selective palladium-catalyzed allylic oxidation reactions.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Yu|first1=Jin-Quan|last2=Corey|first2=E. J.|date=2002-08-01|title=Diverse Pathways for the Palladium(II)-Mediated Oxidation of Olefins by tert-Butylhydroperoxide|url=https://doi.org/10.1021/ol0262340|journal=Organic Letters|volume=4|issue=16|pages=2727–2730|doi=10.1021/ol0262340|pmid=12153220 |issn=1523-7060|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Yu|first1=Jin-Quan|last2=Corey|first2=E. J.|date=2003-03-01|title=A Mild, Catalytic, and Highly Selective Method for the Oxidation of α,β-Enones to 1,4-Enediones|url=https://doi.org/10.1021/ja0340735|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=125|issue=11|pages=3232–3233|doi=10.1021/ja0340735|pmid=12630876 |bibcode=2003JAChS.125.3232Y |issn=0002-7863|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Yu|first1=Jin-Quan|last2=Wu|first2=Hai-Chen|last3=Corey|first3=E. J.|date=2005-03-01|title=Pd(OH)2/C-Mediated Selective Oxidation of Silyl Enol Ethers by tert-Butylhydroperoxide, a Useful Method for the Conversion of Ketones to α,β-Enones or β-Silyloxy-α,β-enones|url=https://doi.org/10.1021/ol050284y|journal=Organic Letters|volume=7|issue=7|pages=1415–1417|doi=10.1021/ol050284y|pmid=15787520 |issn=1523-7060|url-access=subscription}}</ref> Yu returned to Cambridge in 2002 and continued in his position as a Junior Research Fellow.<ref name=":5">{{Cite web|title=The Yu Lab|url=https://www.scripps.edu/yu/jqy.html|access-date=2021-05-23|website=www.scripps.edu}}</ref>

== Independent career ==
Yu was awarded a [[Royal Society University Research Fellowship]] in 2003, which allowed him to start his independent research towards the development of asymmetric C–H activation reactions.<ref name=":5" /><ref name=":0" /> In 2004, he moved to [[Brandeis University]] as an assistant professor of chemistry.<ref name=":5" /> He moved to [[The Scripps Research Institute]] as an associate professor in 2007 and was promoted to full professor in 2010. In 2012, he was appointed the Frank and Bertha Hupp Professor of Chemistry.<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":0" />

== Research ==<!--I'm not an expert on Yu's contributions to the C-H activation field. If someone else is able to write a more compelling, neutral summary of Yu's contributions to the field, that would be much appreciated!-->

Yu is an organic synthetic chemist who develops of new methods for functionalizing carbon-hydrogen (C–H) bonds, or [[Carbon–hydrogen bond activation|C–H activation]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Yu|first=Jin-Quan|date=2014|title=Directed C–H Activation Reactions of Synthetically Versatile Substrates: A Journey to Practicality|journal=Advanced Synthesis & Catalysis|language=en|volume=356|issue=7|pages=1393|doi=10.1002/adsc.201400406|issn=1615-4169|doi-access=}}</ref> A longstanding goal in organic synthesis, C–H activation would allow for inert, unreactive C–H bonds to be replaced with bonds to [[Functional group|functional groups]] that can alter a molecule's reactivity and properties. One strategy to achieve selective C–H activation under mild conditions is to use metal-based catalysts that are guided to the targeted C–H bond by nearby directing functional groups. These directing groups often must be removed once the new functional group has been appended to the molecule.<ref name=":3" /> This style of C–H activation methodology could greatly simplify the synthesis of [[Medication|pharmaceutical drug molecules]], [[Agrochemical|agrochemicals]], and [[Natural product|natural products]].

Yu has contributed metal palladium-catalyzed C-H bond activation promoted by "weak coordination," that is by directing group effects.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Engle|first1=Keary M.|last2=Mei|first2=Tian-Sheng|last3=Wasa|first3=Masayuki|last4=Yu|first4=Jin-Quan|date=2011-12-14|title=Weak Coordination as a Powerful Means for Developing Broadly Useful C–H Functionalization Reactions|journal=Accounts of Chemical Research|volume=45|issue=6|pages=788–802|doi=10.1021/ar200185g|issn=0001-4842|pmc=3334399|pmid=22166158}}</ref> Other areas of interest are the development of remote C-H bond activation, for example at the [[Meta-selective C–H functionalization|meta-position]] to a directing group.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Leow|first1=Dasheng|last2=Li|first2=Gang|last3=Mei|first3=Tian-Sheng|last4=Yu|first4=Jin-Quan|date=2012|title=Activation of remote meta-C–H bonds assisted by an end-on template|journal=Nature|language=En|volume=486|issue=7404|pages=518–522|doi=10.1038/nature11158|issn=0028-0836|pmc=3386562|pmid=22739317|bibcode=2012Natur.486..518L }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Zhang|first1=Zhipeng|last2=Tanaka|first2=Keita|last3=Yu|first3=Jin-Quan|date=2017|title=Remote site-selective C–H activation directed by a catalytic bifunctional template|journal=Nature|language=en|volume=543|issue=7646|pages=538–542|doi=10.1038/nature21418|pmid=28273068 |issn=1476-4687|pmc=5477648|bibcode=2017Natur.543..538Z }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Wang|first1=Xiao-Chen|last2=Gong|first2=Wei|last3=Fang|first3=Li-Zhen|last4=Zhu|first4=Ru-Yi|last5=Li|first5=Suhua|last6=Engle|first6=Keary M.|last7=Yu|first7=Jin-Quan|date=2015|title=Ligand-enabled meta-C–H activation using a transient mediator|journal=Nature|language=En|volume=519|issue=7543|pages=334–338|doi=10.1038/nature14214|issn=0028-0836|pmc=4368492|pmid=25754328|bibcode=2015Natur.519..334W }}</ref> Since many drugs and natural products are chiral, Yu has also developed important asymmetric C-H bond activation reactions, including those templated by modified amino acids that can act as transient, chiral directing groups.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Saint-Denis|first1=Tyler G.|last2=Zhu|first2=Ru-Yi|last3=Chen|first3=Gang|last4=Wu|first4=Qing-Feng|last5=Yu|first5=Jin-Quan|date=2018-02-16|title=Enantioselective C(sp3)‒H bond activation by chiral transition metal catalysts|journal=Science|language=en|volume=359|issue=6377|doi=10.1126/science.aao4798|issn=0036-8075|pmid=29449462|pmc=5862070}}</ref><ref>{{Cite == Awards and memberships ==
Yu is the recipient of numerous awards and honors for his work in organic chemistry reaction development, including a MacArthur Fellowship (also known as a "Genius Grant") in 2016.<ref name=":3" /> He was elected a member of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 2019,<ref name=":4" /> a fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] and the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] in 2012.<ref name=":5" /> In 2013, he received the [[Sackler Prize|Raymond and Beverly Sackler Prize in the Physical Sciences]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=CCHF {{!}} Event Report|url=https://www.nsf-cchf.com/events/2013_06_jqysackler.html|access-date=2021-05-23|website=www.nsf-cchf.com}}</ref>

Yu received the [[List of Royal Society of Chemistry medals and awards|Pedler Award from the Royal Society of Chemistry]] in 2016,<ref>{{Cite web|date=2018-03-23|title=EuCheMS Chemistry Congress plenary speakers: Jin-Quan Yu|url=https://www.rsc.org/news-events/profiles/2018/mar/jin-quan-yu/|access-date=2021-05-23|website=Royal Society of Chemistry|language=en-GB}}</ref> and the [[List of American Chemical Society national awards|Elias J. Corey Award for Outstanding Original Contribution in Organic Synthesis by a Young Investigator]] from the American Chemical Society.<ref>{{Cite web|title=CCHF {{!}} Event Report|url=https://www.nsf-cchf.com/events/2015_03_jqyCorey.html#:~:text=Jin-Quan%20Yu%20was%20awarded,Synthesis%20by%20a%20Young%20Investigator.|access-date=2021-05-23|website=www.nsf-cchf.com}}</ref> In 2012, he was awarded the Mukaiyama Award from the Japanese Society of Organic Synthesis,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Mukaiyama Award {{!}} SSOCJ {{!}} The Society of Synthetic Organic Chemistry, Japan|url=https://www.ssocj.jp/en/award/mukaiyama-award/|access-date=2021-05-23|website=Mukaiyama Award {{!}} SSOCJ {{!}} The Society of Synthetic Organic Chemistry, Japan|language=en}}</ref> the [[List of American Chemical Society national awards|ACS Cope Scholar Award]],<ref>{{Cite web|last=Drahl|first=Carmen|date=February 27, 2012|title=Arthur C. Cope Scholar: Jin-Quan Yu|url=https://cen.acs.org/articles/90/i9/Arthur-C-Cope-Scholar-Jin.html|access-date=2021-05-23|website=cen.acs.org}}</ref> and the [[Bristol Myers Squibb|Bristol-Myers Squibb]] Award.<ref name=":5" /> His honors also include the [[Novartis]] Early Career Award in Organic Chemistry (2011),<ref>{{Cite web|title=Novartis Early Career Award in Organic Chemistry 2011 :: News :: ChemistryViews|url=https://www.chemistryviews.org/details/news/1416497/Novartis_Early_Career_Award_in_Organic_Chemistry_2011.html|access-date=2021-05-23|website=www.chemistryviews.org}}</ref> [[Eli Lilly]] Grantee Award (2008), [[Amgen]] Young Investigator's Award (2008),<ref name=":5" /> and [[Sloan Research Fellowship]] (2008).<ref>{{Cite web|title=2008 Annual Report - Alfred P. Sloan Foundation|url=https://sloan.org/storage/app/media/files/annual_reports/2008_annual_report_vf.pdf}}</ref> In 2026, Yu was elected to the [[National Academy of Sciences]]<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 28, 2026|title=National Academy of Sciences Elects Members and International Members - NAS|url=https://www.nasonline.org/news/2026-nas-election/|url-status=live|access-date=2026-05-06|website=National Academy of Sciences|language=en-US}}</ref> and elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-05-27|title=Exceptional scientists elected as Fellows of the Royal Society|url=https://royalsociety.org/news/2026/05/new-fellows-announcement-2026/|access-date=2026-05-31|website=Royal Society|language=en}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Yu has a daughter, Anna, and a son, Tony.<ref name=":1" />
